C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2.Summary: Close `F240` and `F245` in one bundle: the review surface stops calling a plan's own declared future a present-tense lie, and stops attributing a bundle's own third authoring artifact to the executor. Implements the roadmap `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` — the governed path is the path of least resistance. This is **V1** of the maintainer's recorded sequence of 2026-09-13, "V1 then V2": V1 pays `F240` and `F245` inside `src/review/core.ts`, its suite, and the catalog copy, and mints this bundle's own registry row to pay both findings at the close. **V2** — the next teaching increment, the executors' `SKILL GAPS`, `F243` — is a later bundle and is a NonGoal here. No new `review.*` code, no new CLI token, no schema or serializer change, no version bump, no teaching-surface edit. **Two deliverables, one file plus its suite, and the row that pays them.** (1) The `<MustExist>` walk in `detectConfidentlyWrong` (`src/review/core.ts:470`, present at `3bbc8ed`) reads every active plan's `MustExist` against present disk, Baseline and Target alike, with no exemption for a path the plan itself declares it will write; the remedy chosen here is to exempt a Target `MustExist` whose path the plan's own declared write scope names, only while the plan is not yet `applied`. (2) The identity skip `isReviewedChangeSpecOrPlanPath` (`:1037`) exempts the reviewed change's own `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` in both locations — four paths; the bundle contract in `ngrace-spec` names `design-context.xml` as the bundle's third artifact, so the skip extends to it in both locations. (3) The record row `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2` pays `F240` and `F245`; both findings and the row move at the close.
C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2.Problem:
**`F240` — a file-creating bundle carries review errors from plan-approve until its first task lands.** Measured 2026-09-12 at `34072ef`, plan-approve of `C-APPLY-VERB`. Re-measured at `3bbc8ed` on a throwaway copy: an active plan whose `TargetAssertions` claim `<MustExist>` on a file it exists to create reports `review.confidently-wrong` against present disk, before any task has run. `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND`'s ledger holds the cost: the findings stood at plan-approve, vanished when the target landed, and were never acked, so the record shows a clean review that was never clean at approval. A Target assertion is an end state; reading it against present disk before execution is the category error the detector's own name makes explicit. `F240` records the question and the owner: "the bundle that next opens `src/review/core.ts`" — this bundle is that opener.
**`F245` — the identity skip's third artifact.** Measured 2026-09-13 at `d84e37a` by the executor authoring `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY/plan.xml`. A bundle that writes the optional companion the `ngrace-spec` skill defines was reported out of scope on its own `design-context.xml` and had to declare its own authoring artifact in `ObservedWriteScope` to get a clean review. Re-measured at `3bbc8ed` on a throwaway copy: with `--changed-files` naming a reviewed bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml` and `design-context.xml`, exactly one finding appears — on `design-context.xml`. The skip is an identity-keyed sibling predicate of `isCliLifecyclePath`; extending it adds a leaf to a predicate that is *already* identity-keyed, and never widens the shared lifecycle helper.
**Both changes overturn shipped behaviour, and a spec that does not say so is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` rule 9 exists to prevent.** The four-path skip was written by `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION` (PR #71, `475aee6`) on `F155`'s argument, and `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION-2` re-established it after a supersede: the exemption is identity-keyed, `isCliLifecyclePath` is never widened because `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` shares it, and the alias-expansion property was deliberately re-vehicled onto `design-context.xml` *because that path was not skipped*. The `<MustExist>`-on-disk walk's shipped criteria (C-REVIEW-SURFACE `AC-REVIEW-PATTERN-DETECTORS` and its corpus row `corpus-cw-02`; C-BOUND-VERDICT `AC-F123`; C-REVIEW-ARCHIVE-SCOPE `AC-CW-KEPT`) require an approved or applied plan's absent `MustExist` to keep firing. The constraints below name every criterion each change overturns and answer its original argument.
**How this bundle exists.** Its substance is the approved spec of `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE`, ratified twice, whose archived copy stands at `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE/spec.xml`. The bundle was superseded for its plan, not this spec's substance: the approved plan carried a `BaselineAssertions` `MustNotContain` on `src/review/core.ts` for a string two other detectors already contain (`:589` in `detectSelfReferential`, `:824` in `detectZeroOrMoreSwallow`), so the needle was false at HEAD from the moment of approval and no execution could satisfy it (F246). D27 and the `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2` profile rule that an approved governance artifact is repaired by `ngrace supersede` and a replacement bundle, never amend-and-re-ratify, so the whole bundle was archived under `<Replacement>C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2</Replacement>` with zero code discarded. This spec carries that approved substance forward under the new name with the bundle's identity sentences rewritten and the mint-search figures re-derived at `370ed79` (the record Constraint); the archived bundle is immutable and nothing in it is edited.

Goals.Goal: **F240 remedy, chosen: exempt a Target `<MustExist>` whose path the plan's own declared write scope names, in the un-applied window only.** The declared write scope is the plan's `<ObservedWriteScope>`: children `<File>` and `<Path>` (files) and `<Glob>` (globs), exactly the set `extractObservedWriteScopeFromPlan` (`src/review/scope-helpers.ts`) reads and `observedWriteScopeContains` (`src/artifact/scope.ts:133`) matches. **Globs count**: the exemption is decided by `observedWriteScopeContains`, whose glob arm parses the GRACE scope-glob grammar, so a `<Glob>src/probe/*.ts</Glob>` declaration exempts a Target under it (driven). The exemption holds only while the plan's root status is **not** `applied`; an `applied` plan's Target `<MustExist>`, active or archived, stays a real check against HEAD. `BaselineAssertions` `<MustExist>` is never exempt. The predicate axis is the plan's own root **status** for this detector, not its location: a plan that is `applied` but still under `changes/active/` (the window between the apply status write and the archive move) has present-tree Target obligations and must still fire (driven — the location-gated variant silences it, which is the runner-up's loss).

**F245 remedy: extend the identity skip to the bundle's third authoring artifact.** `isReviewedChangeSpecOrPlanPath` skips the reviewed change's own `design-context.xml` under `changes/active/<id>/` and `changes/archive/<id>/`, in addition to the four `spec.xml` / `plan.xml` paths it already skips, keyed on the same `identity.changeId`. It stays a sibling predicate of `isCliLifecyclePath`: `isCliLifecyclePath` is **not** widened, and `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` keeps raising on an undeclared bundle artifact recorded in the executor's ledger. `F155`'s breach signal is intact: a foreign bundle's `design-context.xml` still fires (driven on both the helper and the CLI).

**The catalog copy states the narrowed check and the three-artifact skip.** Today `review.confidently-wrong` (`src/review/catalog.ts:87`) says only that an existence claim is asserted without production evidence, and `review.scope-outside-write-scope` (`:164`) says only that a changed path is outside `ObservedWriteScope` — neither describes the Baseline-versus-Target narrowing or the identity skip. Their `explanation` / `remediation` text gains one sentence each; their `title`, `code`, `severity`, `derivedFrom` and `family` are unchanged, and `src/grace-lint.test.ts:1734`'s title pin stays green.

**The record row and the close move.** `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2` is minted as a live `kind="chartered"` row in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry.xml` with `<Pays>F240 F245</Pays>` and a `<StatusText>` naming no `F` token, then one shipped `--rewrite-roots` re-derives every base and holds every ceiling. At the close, one shipped `--retire` moves `F240` and `F245` to `findings-retired.xml` stamped `<PaidBy>C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2</PaidBy>`, flips both index `Entry` layers in place, and moves the row to `registry-retired.xml`. No record engine edit, no hand-written `<PaidBy>`, no ceiling raised, no `--split`.

Read the plan's status; derive `unapplied = planStatus !== "applied"`. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-F240-PAIR:
The narrowed `<MustExist>` check discriminates. `SILENT`: an active plan with root status `approved` whose `TargetAssertions` hold `<MustExist>` on a path its own `<ObservedWriteScope>` names (`<File>`, `<Path>`, or `<Glob>`) and the path is absent on disk yields no `review.confidently-wrong` for that target. `FIRE`: the same shape with the path **not** declared yields exactly that finding, and a `BaselineAssertions` `<MustExist>` on an absent path yields it too. Failure conditions: the declared Target still fires; the undeclared Target or the Baseline goes silent; the skip is keyed on `planLocation` rather than status; a `<Glob>`-declared target still fires. Instrument: `detectConfidentlyWrong` / `runPatternDetectors` over temporary roots; red observed on a throwaway copy in both directions with the remedy present.
